review_output: {"summary":"In scope: cache scope and lifetime, and database cancellation classification, in two files. Nothing blocks. The facade's cache correctly ties the cached context to the callback object, matches on the full scope key, caches an unavailable context too, and removes the entry when the callback ends. The 57014 and P2028 handling throws away partial results and only maps the narrow cases, rethrowing everything else. Two minor defects: the per-page revision check can never fail, and the facade does not actually restrict which scope it serves. Whether Prisma reports 57014 under P2010 meta.code, and what text a real P2028 expiry produces, depends on the Prisma version. That version wasn't supplied, so I didn't count it as a defect.","findings":[{"severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.9,"area":"cache scope/lifetime","file":"src/lib/live-metric-order-source-audit.ts","issue":"The per-page revision check can never fail. Every page call through the facade gets its revisions from the context cached once at the start, so `current` is always equal to `revisions`.","evidence":"audit.ts:17-18 returns cached.context when the scope key matches, and :47 spreads that same object into every page. source-audit.ts:31-32 compares those values, so the 'snapshot revision changed' error can never be thrown.","impact":"The check suggests the revisions are re-read during the transaction, but they aren't. Someone could rely on it as a consistency guard. Under RR the values would normally match anyway, so this is a misleading-control problem, not a data-correctness bug.","recommended_fix":"Either delete the comparison and state that revisions are captured once per snapshot, or deliberately re-read the revisions on the final page (skipping the cache) and compare them to the cached context.","required_test":"A unit test that makes a later page or a final re-read return different revisions, and asserts that the audit throws or returns unavailable. Today this test cannot be written against the cached path, which confirms the gap."},{"severity":"NIT","confidence":0.7,"area":"cache scope","file":"src/lib/live-metric-order-audit.ts","issue":"The facade comment says it 'owns one validated scope', but a page read through the snapshot with a different scope silently runs a fresh readAuditContext instead of being rejected.","evidence":"audit.ts:18 falls back to readAuditContext(tx, input) when the key doesn't match, and the doc at :59 claims a single scope per facade.","impact":"Nothing is reused across scopes, so this is not a leak (consistent with your cross-tenant and time-window tests). But the facade enforces less than its comment says, and any reader using a mismatched scope pays for an extra context query on every page.","recommended_fix":"When the client is a registered facade and the scope key doesn't match, throw or return unavailable. Alternatively, reword the comment.","required_test":"Inside withMetricOrderAuditContext, call readMetricOrderAuditPage on the snapshot with a different vendorId or window, and assert that it is rejected."}]}
